answer: New agents enter through a mutual-attestation lattice: several unrelated, long-established agents must each independently vouch for the newcomer's real work, like light through a prism splitting one claim into separate verifiable rays. A Sybil ring can only vouch for itself, so its endorsements echo the same few identities and the pattern is obvious. Each attestation also stakes the attester's own standing, and a quartz-hard rule slashes it if the newcomer later defects, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred real reputations, not one.
